identityLeakageWarning: Names, places and exact dates are removed where practical. Pretraining may still reveal identity; identity/future-theory leakage is audited separately and never rewarded.

cases.cutoff: after radio reflection/detection feasibility is accepted for aircraft warning, before an operational national radar chain and before the high-power cavity magnetron

packet.pressure: A country exposed to fast bomber attack needs warning beyond visual range. Radio experiments indicate aircraft can disturb/reflect radio energy, but available sets are long-wavelength, bulky and relatively coarse. Warning is useful only if detections arrive early enough to change interception decisions.
availableEvidence: Aircraft speed makes visual/acoustic warning alone increasingly late.
Long-wavelength radio transmitters/receivers can detect large aircraft at useful distances in trials, but angular/altitude precision is limited.
Telephone/radio reporting, plotting rooms, observers and fighter units already exist separately but are not yet one integrated detection-to-action network.
Shorter wavelengths promise better angular resolution and smaller antennas, but available sources at those wavelengths have much lower practical power.
Fixed coastal stations are easier to build quickly than compact airborne/mobile systems.
liveRoutes: deploy a chain of fixed long-wavelength warning stations and integrate them with reporting/plotting/interception while improving them iteratively
delay deployment until a high-power short-wavelength source exists and pursue precision first
expand acoustic/visual observer networks as the main warning system
build a few experimental radio sets but keep them separate from command operations until measurement accuracy is much higher
pursue both deployable coarse warning and a separate research line for higher-frequency compact radar
constraints: deployment time matters because the threat is near-term
false alarms and missed detections have operational cost
radio hardware/manufacturing capacity is finite
a detector without communications/decision integration may not change outcomes
future microwave sources are not yet available

cases.hiddenOutcome: A fixed long-wavelength warning chain is deployed and, when integrated into an air-defence reporting/command network, provides operationally valuable early warning despite coarse technical resolution. In 1940 a high-power cavity magnetron changes the later frontier, enabling compact high-resolution microwave radar and transatlantic industrialization.

cases.cutoff: after nuclear fission and secondary-neutron multiplication are recognized as physically plausible, before a controlled self-sustaining pile exists

packet.pressure: A newly recognized nuclear process splits heavy nuclei and releases energy plus additional neutrons. A self-sustaining chain appears possible, but neutron losses, moderator absorption, material purity and isotope composition are uncertain. The stakes of a false positive or premature industrial commitment are enormous.
availableEvidence: Neutron-induced fission of uranium is now accepted and multiple neutrons can emerge from events.
Natural uranium contains multiple isotopes with different likely roles, but exact engineering implications remain uncertain.
Graphite and heavy water are candidate moderators; trace impurities can strongly affect neutron economy.
Small exponential/pile experiments can measure neutron multiplication without building a full critical system.
Isotope-separation methods exist in principle but are technically difficult and expensive.
A low-power controlled chain reaction, if achieved, would still not establish heat removal, radiation shielding or industrial material production.
liveRoutes: build a sequence of subcritical lattice/pile experiments to measure neutron multiplication and material purity before approaching criticality
commit immediately to a full production reactor using the best current graphite/uranium estimates
pursue isotope enrichment in parallel because the reactor route may fail
pursue a heavy-water moderated route in parallel
stop after demonstrating one fission event because the basic physics is already proven
separate proof-of-controlled-chain-reaction from later production-reactor engineering rather than treating them as one scale step
constraints: criticality errors can be dangerous
high-purity moderator/fuel supply is limited
full industrial plants are extremely expensive
wartime schedule creates value for parallelism/redundancy
post-criticality thermal/radiation/chemical-separation problems are outside the small-pile evidence

cases.hiddenOutcome: Intermediate pile experiments refine neutron-economy/material requirements; a low-power graphite/uranium pile achieves the first controlled self-sustaining chain reaction in 1942. Production then becomes a new frontier involving cooling, shielding, poisoning, reactor control and chemical separation, while multiple enrichment/material-production routes remain parallel because uncertainty and schedule value justify redundancy.

cases.cutoff: after purified antibacterial material has cured systemic infection in mice, before convincing human treatment and before industrial-scale production

packet.pressure: A mold-derived antibacterial substance has been purified enough to rescue infected mice. It is unstable, difficult to recover, and available only in tiny quantities. Existing sulfonamide drugs are already clinically useful. The question is whether to turn this fragile laboratory effect into a human therapy and how to make enough material to test/use it.
availableEvidence: The original mold observation is more than a decade old and did not itself produce a practical drug.
A research group has improved extraction/purification enough to show systemic therapeutic effect in infected mice.
Current yields are extremely low; large volumes of surface culture would be needed for even a small number of patients.
The substance appears relatively non-toxic in the animal work, but human dosing/effect are not yet established.
Fermentation performance depends on strain, medium, oxygen transfer and recovery chemistry, but no proven mass-production process exists.
Sulfonamides provide a strong simpler therapeutic baseline for some infections.
liveRoutes: spend scarce purified material on a tightly monitored human therapeutic test while continuing purification
continue only animal experiments until a large production process exists
scale the current shallow-surface fermentation directly without changing strain/media/process
run parallel strain/medium/fermentation-process searches while preserving a clinical-validation stream
abandon the substance because sulfonamides are already deployable
treat production as a separate experimental frontier rather than routine manufacturing
constraints: material is extremely scarce
systemic human infection can be lethal and evidence must justify exposure
sterility/purity/dosing matter
industrial fermentation equipment exists but this organism/process is not yet proven at scale
wartime demand may justify parallel clinical and process development

cases.hiddenOutcome: Early human treatment provides dramatic evidence but supply remains severe. British/U.S. collaboration then opens a separate production frontier: strain search, media such as corn steep liquor, aeration/agitation and deep-tank fermentation plus industrial recovery expand output by orders of magnitude. Sulfonamides remain useful comparators while penicillin scale catches up.

cases.cutoff: after repetitive cipher-search/statistical workloads and reliable relay/vacuum-tube logic are available, before Colossus or ENIAC are operational and before a mature stored-program architecture

packet.pressure: Wartime analysts face huge repetitive search/counting workloads. One class of cipher problems can be reduced to checking many candidate settings against logical/statistical constraints; numerical table production also exceeds human clerical capacity. Existing electromechanical machines help but are too slow for some time-sensitive workloads.
availableEvidence: A prior allied team has shown that mathematical structure can reduce a mechanized cipher to constrained search rather than brute force every message.
Electromechanical relay machines can automate repeated tests but mechanical switching limits speed.
Vacuum-tube circuits can switch/count much faster and have been reliable in communications equipment, though thousands of tubes raise maintenance concerns.
High-speed paper-tape/photoelectric input is technically plausible for streaming intercepted symbols.
Human analysts are still needed to choose hypotheses/cribs, prepare data, interpret outputs and change the search logic.
Large numerical electronic calculators are conceptually plausible, but electronic reconfiguration and hardware cost are substantial.
liveRoutes: scale human clerical analysis and add more operators
build more electromechanical special-purpose search machines using known cipher structure
build a special-purpose electronic statistical/counting machine fed by high-speed tape while humans set tests
attempt an all-purpose autonomous machine that discovers cipher structure without human hypotheses
develop a large electronic numerical calculator for table production as a separate workload
treat human analysis, machine search and operational interpretation as one coupled workflow and optimize the current bottleneck rather than demanding generality
constraints: results lose value if they arrive after operational decisions
secrecy limits normal peer review and diffusion
vacuum-tube reliability and maintenance are real engineering risks
program logic may require manual plug/switch setup
transistors, modern programming languages and mature stored-program computers are unavailable

cases.hiddenOutcome: Special-purpose electromechanical and electronic machines prove highly valuable when embedded in human cryptanalytic workflows. A vacuum-tube electronic machine becomes operational in 1944 for a narrow statistical cipher task, while a separate U.S. electronic numerical machine demonstrates great arithmetic speed but laborious manual reconfiguration. Stored-program organization emerges as a later architecture; wartime impact did not require autonomy or one universal machine.
